# lookbook

Distill raw image pools into optimized, high-diversity reference sets for training personalized models (character LoRAs, product LoRAs, style LoRAs).

## Install

```bash
pip install lookbook                  # core: Pillow, numpy, dol, meshed, config2py
pip install lookbook[funnel]          # + cv2 / imagededup for the cheap funnel
pip install lookbook[embed]           # + torch, CLIP, DINOv2, pyiqa, apricot
pip install lookbook[person]          # + InsightFace, head pose, mediapipe
pip install lookbook[http]            # + FastAPI / qh server
pip install lookbook[mcp]             # + fastmcp (Anthropic MCP server)
```

The base install has no ML dependencies — Phase 1 (cheap funnel) works on a plain laptop. `[embed]` and beyond pull torch.

## Quickstart

CLI:

```bash
# Phase 1: clean up a photo dump (drops blurry, dark, duplicate, tiny).
lookbook curate ./photos --k 20 --recipe funnel

# Phase 2: same funnel + DINOv2 embeddings + facility-location selection
# for "diverse but sharp" picks. Downloads ~350MB on first run; subsequent
# runs are fast and cached. Use --recipe diverse_clip for CLIP semantic
# embeddings instead.
lookbook curate ./photos --k 20 --recipe diverse

# Phase 3: full character/person LoRA curation. Detects faces, embeds
# with ArcFace, applies pose-bin quotas, and runs cluster-coverage
# diagnosis. Pulls insightface + sixdrepnet (lazy on first use).
lookbook curate ./photos --k 20 --recipe person

# Same shape with no model downloads (mock backends; useful for tests):
lookbook curate ./photos --k 8 --recipe person_mock

# Phase 4: HTTP server. Every verb is POST /<verb> with a JSON body;
# Swagger UI at /docs.
lookbook serve --port 8000 --host 127.0.0.1
# curl examples:
#   curl -X POST localhost:8000/list_recipes -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
#   curl -X POST localhost:8000/curate_source -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
#        -d '{"source_path":"/abs/photos","k":20,"recipe":"funnel"}'

# Phase 5: MCP server (stdio transport — for Claude Desktop, Anthropic SDK).
# Each verb is exposed as an MCP tool an agent can call.
lookbook mcp

# See available scorers, embedders, filters, selectors, recipes / profiles:
lookbook list-plugins
lookbook list-recipes
```

Python:

```python
from lookbook import curate

result = curate(
    "./photos",
    k=20,
    scorer_ids=("resolution", "file_hash", "phash", "blur", "exposure"),
    filter_ids=(
        ("min_resolution", {"min_long_side": 800}),
        "exposure_range",
        "min_blur",
        "no_exact_duplicate",
        "no_near_duplicate",
    ),
    selector_id=("top_k", {"metric_id": "blur"}),
)
print(result.report)  # drop counts attributed to each filter
print([r.image_id for r in result.kept])
```

### One-call presets: character and environment references

Two opinionated facades over `curate` for the “pick the best reference image(s) from this pool” job:

```python
from lookbook import curate_for_character, curate_for_environment

# Known character: scores resolution / sharpness / exposure / face quality,
# ranks by the composite `face_quality`. face_detector="mock_face" runs it
# offline; the default "insightface" needs `pip install lookbook[person]`.
best = curate_for_character("./frames", k=1)

# No-face pools (environment plates, props, style boards): ranks by the
# composite `technical_quality`. No ML dependency at all.
best = curate_for_environment("./plates", k=3)
```

### Identity check: does this generation still match the reference?

<!-- wads-docs: skip needs a reference image from the reader -->
```python
from lookbook import compare_to_reference

result = compare_to_reference(reference, candidate, embedder="arcface")
result.score  # [0, 1], 1 = same identity
result.passed  # score >= threshold (0.85 default) — advisory
result.per_reference  # per-view breakdown when the reference is a pool
```

`reference` is one image ref or a list of them (folded by `aggregation`, `"max"` by default). Use `"clip"` / `"dinov2"` as the embedder for scenes, props and architecture. Also exposed as `POST /compare_to_reference` and as the `compare_to_reference` MCP tool.

### Interactive curate (keep the human in the loop)

Pipeline-only top-k can rank “boring but sharp” above “stylistically perfect but slightly blurry”. `curate_interactive` invites the caller into the loop, one round at a time:

```python
from lookbook import curate_interactive, InteractiveDecision


def decide(presented, info):
    # show `presented` to the user; collect their picks
    return InteractiveDecision(keep=("img-abc",), reject=("img-xyz",))


result = curate_interactive(
    "./photos",
    on_decision=decide,
    k=20,
    present=8,
    scorer_ids=("blur", "exposure"),
)
```

Pre-recorded decisions (a list of `InteractiveDecision`) are accepted in place of the callable — handy for tests, headless replays, and agent-scripted flows.

### `local_path()` on every ImageRef

`PathImageRef`, `BytesImageRef`, and `UrlImageRef` all expose `local_path(cache_dir=None) -> str`. Path refs return their existing path; bytes/url refs materialize once into a content-addressed cache (honors `$LOOKBOOK_REFS_CACHE_DIR`). The free function `lookbook.to_local_path(ref)` dispatches across all subtypes — useful when downstream tools (ffmpeg, fal upload) need a real file.

## Why

Training a personalized image model needs ~15–30 carefully chosen reference images, where each adds new context — pose, lighting, expression, distance. “Top-K by score” collapses to near-duplicates; this is fundamentally a *set-selection* problem with diversity as a constraint, not a tiebreaker.

`lookbook` separates **per-image scoring** (is this image individually good?) from **set-level selection** (does this collection cover the concept?), and makes both extensible.

## Status

All five v1 phases are shipped. The package can: clean a photo dump (200→20 in <30s, no GPU); run the full embeddings + facility-location workflow with CLIP or DINOv2; curate a person / character LoRA with face detection, ArcFace identity diversity, and pose-bin quotas; serve every verb over HTTP (FastAPI via `qh`); and expose every verb over MCP (via `fastmcp`) so an LLM agent can drive curation directly. Since then it has also gained one-call character / environment reference picks, a human-in-the-loop `curate_interactive`, and `compare_to_reference` — “is this generation still the same subject?” as a number. See [`misc/docs/lookbook_development_plan.md`]() for the full roadmap and [`misc/docs/lookbook_design_report.md`]() for the design rationale.

## Architecture

Five layers; the heavy ML libs live only at the bottom so the upper layers stay laptop-installable.

```default
Interface       (CLI, HTTP via qh, MCP via fastmcp, Python lib)
   ↓
Recipe / facade (lookbook.curate, named recipes, profiles)
   ↓
Orchestration  (lookbook.pipeline, manifest, drop attribution, run records)
   ↓
Plugin layer   (Scorer | Filter | Embedder | Selector — Protocols)
   ↓
Backend        (CLIP, DINOv2, InsightFace, 6DRepNet — wrapped, lazy-imported)
```

The **manifest** — `MutableMapping[(image_id, metric_id), Annotation]` — is the SSOT. Persistence is pluggable via `dol`: filesystem (default), SQLite, S3, Mongo, Redis. The default location is the user’s app data folder via `config2py`: `~/.local/share/lookbook` on Linux *and* macOS (it follows the XDG convention, not `~/Library/Application Support`), `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows.

New scorers/selectors/filters are *registered*, never subclassed. See the `.claude/skills/` directory for developer skills (`lookbook-dev`, `lookbook-add-scorer`, `lookbook-add-selector`, `lookbook-storage`).

## Project layout

```default
lookbook/
  base.py               Protocols + Annotation + Manifest type
  store.py              dol-backed Stores bundle, manifest codec
  _paths.py             config2py-backed default folders
  refs.py               PathImageRef, BytesImageRef, UrlImageRef
  manifest.py           Manifest helpers
  registry.py           Plugin registries
  pipeline.py           Orchestrator (topo-sorted scorers + filters + selector)
  facade.py             curate, score, curate_for_character/environment
  interactive.py        curate_interactive + InteractiveDecision
  report.py             Drop-attributing Report
  scorers/              random, resolution, file_hash, phash, blur, exposure,
                          technical_quality
                          + person.py: face detection, area, head pose, quality
                          + identity.py: cross-image identity similarity
  embedders/            mock, clip, dinov2, arcface (lazy-imported)
  filters/              min_resolution, min_blur, exposure_range, dedup
                          + person.py: has_face, single_face_only, min_face_*
  selectors/            top_k, facility_location, quota
  profiles/             person.yaml, person_mock.yaml (+ user-edited via config2py)
  diagnose.py           cluster_coverage (set-level diagnosis)
  io/                   ingest, ingest_to_store
  http.py               qh-built FastAPI surface; mk_lookbook_app, serve
  mcp.py                fastmcp-built MCP server; mk_lookbook_mcp, serve
  __main__.py           CLI (cw): curate, list-plugins, list-recipes

.claude/skills/         Claude Code skills for development & agent use
misc/docs/              Design report + development plan
tests/                  pytest, hermetic
```

## Claude Code skills

The `.claude/skills/` directory ships nine skills covering both ends of the workflow:

**Dev skills** (used while building / extending lookbook):

- `lookbook-dev` — overall architecture, cross-references between modules
- `lookbook-storage` — repository pattern, swapping storage backends
- `lookbook-add-scorer` — adding a new per-image metric
- `lookbook-add-selector` — adding a new set-selection algorithm
- `lookbook-profile` — adding a subject profile (YAML)
- `lookbook-http` — HTTP route layout + adding endpoints

**Usage skills** (for agents driving lookbook to curate):

- `lookbook-curate` — the headline workflow
- `lookbook-diagnose` — interpreting reports, querying the manifest
- `lookbook-recipe` — customizing recipes per-call or via user YAML

# _autosummary/lookbook.diagnose.html.md

# lookbook.diagnose

Set-level diagnosis: what does the kept set cover, what’s missing.

Phase 2 ships cluster-coverage. The function takes the candidate pool and
the kept subset, clusters the candidates by their embeddings, and reports
how many clusters the kept set populates plus which clusters are
empty / underfilled.

This is the read-only counterpart to the selector — same data, different
question. Selectors *choose*; diagnosers *describe*.

### Functions

| [`cluster_coverage`](_autosummary/lookbook.diagnose.html.md#lookbook.diagnose.cluster_coverage)(candidates, kept, embeddings, \*)   | Cluster the candidate embeddings into `n_clusters` and report coverage.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### lookbook.diagnose.cluster_coverage(candidates, kept, embeddings, , n_clusters=12, random_state=0)

Cluster the candidate embeddings into `n_clusters` and report coverage.

Returns a dict with:

> - `n_clusters`: actual number of clusters used (capped at len(candidates))
> - `n_clusters_filled`: clusters with at least one kept image
> - `cluster_sizes_candidates`: list of int, candidate count per cluster
> - `cluster_sizes_kept`: list of int, kept count per cluster
> - `empty_clusters`: list of int (indexes of clusters with zero kept)
> - `underrepresented_clusters`: clusters with kept_count == 0 and
>   candidate_count >= 2 (the meaningful gaps)
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/lookbook.embedders.arcface.html.md

# lookbook.embedders.arcface

ArcFace identity embedder.

ArcFace embeddings are the standard for face *identity* verification —
neither CLIP nor DINOv2 reliably tells you “this is the same person.”
For character-LoRA curation that’s the load-bearing question.

`InsightFaceArcFace` shares the underlying model weights with
`InsightFaceDetect` (both go through the `FaceAnalysis` app). The
embedder reads the `face_box` annotation from the manifest to know where
to crop, then runs ArcFace on that crop.

### Classes

| [`InsightFaceArcFace`](_autosummary/lookbook.embedders.arcface.html.md#lookbook.embedders.arcface.InsightFaceArcFace)([space_id, cost_tier, ...])   | Real ArcFace embeddings via insightface.       |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| [`MockArcFaceEmbedder`](_autosummary/lookbook.embedders.arcface.html.md#lookbook.embedders.arcface.MockArcFaceEmbedder)([space_id, cost_tier, ...])  | Deterministic mock identity embedder, no deps. |

### *class* lookbook.embedders.arcface.InsightFaceArcFace(space_id='arcface', cost_tier=2, model_name='buffalo_l', det_size=640, backend='insightface:arcface')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Real ArcFace embeddings via insightface.

The implementation is intentionally a thin wrapper. `insightface`’s
`FaceAnalysis.get(img)` returns Face objects with `.embedding` already
L2-normalized; we just pick the largest face’s embedding.

The “right” face is the one whose `bbox` overlaps the manifest’s
`face_box` if available; otherwise the largest by area.

#### *property* config_hash *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

changes whenever a setting that affects its output changes.

* **Type:**
  Cache key for this component

#### embed(ref)

Embed `ref` into this embedder’s vector space.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### *class* lookbook.embedders.arcface.MockArcFaceEmbedder(space_id='arcface_mock', cost_tier=1, dim=512, seed=0, backend='lookbook:mock_arcface')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Deterministic mock identity embedder, no deps.

The vector is keyed by `image_id`, so:

- Same image always yields the same vector.
- Different images yield different vectors.
- There is no “same person” signal — different images of one person
  get unrelated vectors. Useful only for orchestration tests.

#### *property* config_hash *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

changes whenever a setting that affects its output changes.

* **Type:**
  Cache key for this component

#### embed(ref)

Embed `ref` into this embedder’s vector space.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

# lookbook.embedders.clip

CLIP embedder via `transformers`.

CLIP is the right embedding for *semantic* similarity (same concept, different
style). It’s also what LAION-Aesthetic-V2 and CLIP-IQA both consume, so when
those scorers land they can share the cached features computed here.

# _autosummary/lookbook.embedders.dinov2.html.md

# lookbook.embedders.dinov2

DINOv2 embedder via `transformers`.

DINOv2 is the right embedding for *visual* similarity (same scene/object,
robust to style). Voxel51’s benchmarks show it outperforming CLIP on image
classification by 5-28 points on natural-image datasets. For curation, that
makes it the better default for “find redundant shots.”

### Classes

| [`DINOv2Embedder`](_autosummary/lookbook.embedders.dinov2.html.md#lookbook.embedders.dinov2.DINOv2Embedder)([space_id, cost_tier, ...])   | Facebook DINOv2 image embeddings via HuggingFace transformers.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

smaller-but-weaker (~85 MB), `facebook/dinov2-large` for stronger
(~1.2 GB).

# _autosummary/lookbook.embedders.html.md

# lookbook.embedders

Embedders: vector representations per image.

Each submodule registers its embedders into `lookbook.registry.embedders`
on import. Heavy ML deps must be lazy-imported inside `embed()`, never at
module top.

We pre-set `USE_TF=0` and `USE_FLAX=0` so that `transformers` does not try
to load TensorFlow or Flax — both can blow up if the user’s environment
has an incompatible numpy ABI. `setdefault` means we never override a user
who explicitly wants those backends.

### Modules

| [`arcface`](_autosummary/lookbook.embedders.arcface.html.md#module-lookbook.embedders.arcface)   | ArcFace identity embedder.                                          |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`clip`](_autosummary/lookbook.embedders.clip.html.md#module-lookbook.embedders.clip)         | CLIP embedder via `transformers`.                                   |
| [`dinov2`](_autosummary/lookbook.embedders.dinov2.html.md#module-lookbook.embedders.dinov2)     | DINOv2 embedder via `transformers`.                                 |
| [`mock`](_autosummary/lookbook.embedders.mock.html.md#module-lookbook.embedders.mock)         | Deterministic mock embedder for tests and end-to-end orchestration. |

# _autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md

# lookbook.facade

High-level facades — the one-call entry points into the pipeline.

`curate` is the general one: ingest a source, run scorers/embedders/filters,
select K. `curate_for_character` and `curate_for_environment` are opinionated
presets over it, and `score` is the single-image, single-metric shortcut.

Everything here is re-exported from `lookbook`, which is where callers should
import it from. Plugins are named, never subclassed: each `*_ids` argument
takes registry names, optionally paired with config overrides as a
`(name, kwargs)` tuple.

### Functions

| [`curate`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.curate)(source, \*[, k, scorer_ids, ...])     | High-level facade: ingest a source, run a pipeline, return the result.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`curate_for_character`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.curate_for_character)(source, \*[, k, ...])   | Curate the best reference image(s) of a *known* character from a pool.   |
| [`curate_for_environment`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.curate_for_environment)(source, \*[, k, ...]) | Curate the best reference image(s) for a non-person subject.             |
| [`resolve_plugin`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.resolve_plugin)(reg, spec, \*[, fresh])       | Look up a plugin from a registry, optionally with config overrides.      |
| [`score`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.score)(ref, \*, metric_id[, stores])          | Score one image against one metric.                                      |

### lookbook.facade.curate(source, , k=20, scorer_ids=('random_score',), embedder_ids=(), filter_ids=(), selector_id='top_k', diagnose_clusters=0, stores=None, constraints=None)

High-level facade: ingest a source, run a pipeline, return the result.

Each plugin id may be either a string (“blur”) or a (name, kwargs)
tuple ((“blur”, {“max_side”: 256})) to override the default config.

`diagnose_clusters > 0` runs cluster-coverage diagnosis after selection
and writes the result into the report’s `notes`.

* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)

### lookbook.facade.curate_for_character(source, , k=1, face_detector='insightface', stores=None, constraints=None)

Curate the best reference image(s) of a *known* character from a pool.

Opinionated facade over [`curate()`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.curate), tuned for the “pick the
reference image of this one character” job (IP-adapter conditioning,
model-sheet seeding): every image is scored for resolution, sharpness,
exposure and face quality, then the top `k` are taken by the
composite `face_quality` metric.

Identity is *not* scored — the pool is assumed to already be one
character, so what matters is which frame shows them most usably: in
focus, well exposed, face clearly visible and well sized. To check
whether a *generation* still matches a locked reference, use
[`lookbook.compare_to_reference()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.compare_to_reference) instead.

`face_detector` names the registered face-box scorer:

- `"insightface"` — real RetinaFace detection; needs
  `pip install lookbook[person]`. The default.
- `"mock_face"` — the deterministic centred-box detector, for tests
  and demos without the ML dependency.

Images with no detected face score `0` and sort last; the pool is
never filtered down to empty, so a small or awkward pool still yields
a best-effort pick.

* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)

### lookbook.facade.curate_for_environment(source, , k=1, stores=None, constraints=None)

Curate the best reference image(s) for a non-person subject.

Opinionated facade over [`curate()`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.curate) for pools where face detection
is moot — environment plates, prop references, style boards. Each
image is scored for resolution, sharpness and exposure, folded into
the composite `technical_quality` metric, and the top `k` are
taken.

Unlike [`curate_for_character()`](_autosummary/lookbook.facade.html.md#lookbook.facade.curate_for_character) this needs no ML dependency — the
scorers run on Pillow + numpy (cv2 is used for sharpness when present,
with a numpy fallback otherwise).

* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)

### lookbook.facade.resolve_plugin(reg, spec, , fresh=False)

Look up a plugin from a registry, optionally with config overrides.

`spec` is either a registered name or a `(name, kwargs)` tuple. With
`fresh=True` (used for filters with internal state), returns a brand
new instance even when no overrides are given.

### lookbook.facade.score(ref, , metric_id, stores=None)

Score one image against one metric. Returns the bare value.

Caches into the manifest so repeated calls are free.

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

# _autosummary/lookbook.filters.person.html.md

# lookbook.filters.person

Person-LoRA filters — Phase 3.

These read `face_box`, `face_area`, and (optionally) `head_pose` from the
manifest. Like all filters in lookbook, they keep an image when the
relevant evidence is missing — the design principle is that filters never
drop on absent annotations.

| [`MinFaceConfidence`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.person.html.md#lookbook.filters.person.MinFaceConfidence)([threshold, name]) | Drop images whose face-detection confidence is below `threshold`.      |
| [`SingleFaceOnly`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.person.html.md#lookbook.filters.person.SingleFaceOnly)([name])               | Drop images with more than one detected face.                          |

# _autosummary/lookbook.filters.technical.html.md

# lookbook.filters.technical

Phase 1 filters — cheap funnel.

Filters consume the manifest and return True/False per image. Two of them
(`NoExactDuplicate`, `NoNearDuplicate`) carry per-pipeline state and must
be re-instantiated for each new run; the rest are stateless.

Each filter exposes a `name` attribute (the filter id) so the run report
can attribute drops back to the rule that fired.

### Functions

| [`fresh_filter`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.technical.html.md#lookbook.filters.technical.fresh_filter)(filter_id, \*\*overrides)   | Return a fresh instance of a registered filter.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`ExposureRange`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.technical.html.md#lookbook.filters.technical.ExposureRange)([max_underexposed_frac, ...])   | Drop images that are mostly black or mostly white.                  |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`MinBlur`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.technical.html.md#lookbook.filters.technical.MinBlur)([threshold, name])                    | Drop images whose Laplacian variance is below `threshold` (blurry). |
| [`MinResolution`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.technical.html.md#lookbook.filters.technical.MinResolution)([min_long_side, name])          | Drop images whose long side is below `min_long_side` pixels.        |
| [`NoExactDuplicate`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.technical.html.md#lookbook.filters.technical.NoExactDuplicate)([name, \_seen])              | Keep at most one image per `file_hash`.                             |
| [`NoNearDuplicate`](_autosummary/lookbook.filters.technical.html.md#lookbook.filters.technical.NoNearDuplicate)([max_distance, name, ...])    | Keep at most one image per near-duplicate cluster.                  |

Reads the `resolution` annotation. If absent, the filter keeps the image
(under the principle that filters never drop on missing evidence).

#### keep(ref, manifest)

Return whether `ref` passes this filter.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### *class* lookbook.filters.technical.NoExactDuplicate(name='no_exact_duplicate', \_seen=set())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Keep at most one image per `file_hash`.

The first image in iteration order to claim a hash wins; later images
with the same hash are dropped.

#### keep(ref, manifest)

Return whether `ref` passes this filter.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### *class* lookbook.filters.technical.NoNearDuplicate(max_distance=5, name='no_near_duplicate', \_seen_hashes=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Keep at most one image per near-duplicate cluster.

Clusters are formed greedily: the first image to be visited is the
cluster representative, and any later image whose `phash` is within
`max_distance` Hamming bits is dropped.

#### keep(ref, manifest)

Return whether `ref` passes this filter.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### lookbook.filters.technical.fresh_filter(filter_id, \*\*overrides)

Return a fresh instance of a registered filter.

Stateful filters (dedup) must be re-instantiated per pipeline; the
registry holds a singleton, so call this when building a fresh pipeline.


# _autosummary/lookbook.html.md

# lookbook

lookbook — distill image pools into reference sets for personalized model training.

Public facade. The package is split across:

- `lookbook.base`      — Protocols and core types (Annotation, Manifest)
- `lookbook.store`     — Repository pattern (Stores) over `dol`
- `lookbook.refs`      — ImageRef implementations
- `lookbook.manifest`  — Manifest helpers
- `lookbook.registry`  — Plugin registries (scorers, filters, embedders, selectors)
- `lookbook.pipeline`  — Pipeline orchestrator
- `lookbook.facade`    — curate / score / curate_for_\* entry points
- `lookbook.interactive` — human-in-the-loop curate loop
- `lookbook.scorers`   — Per-image scorer modules (registered on import)
- `lookbook.selectors` — Selector modules (registered on import)
- `lookbook.io`        — Ingest, export

Plugin registries are accessed as `lookbook.registry.scorers` etc. (not
`lookbook.scorers`, which is the submodule that *holds* scorers).

This module only re-exports; it defines nothing of its own — not even a
`from __future__ import annotations`, so `dir(lookbook)` stays the public API
plus the submodules.

### Functions

| [`compare_to_reference`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.compare_to_reference)(reference_image, ...[, ...])   | Compare a candidate to a reference in one call → [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.SimilarityResult).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`curate`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate)(source, \*[, k, scorer_ids, ...])            | High-level facade: ingest a source, run a pipeline, return the result.                                                |
| [`curate_for_character`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate_for_character)(source, \*[, k, ...])          | Curate the best reference image(s) of a *known* character from a pool.                                                |
| [`curate_for_environment`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate_for_environment)(source, \*[, k, ...])        | Curate the best reference image(s) for a non-person subject.                                                          |
| [`curate_interactive`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate_interactive)(source, \*, on_decision[, ...])  | Run the pipeline in rounds, taking keep/reject decisions per round.                                                   |
| [`get_stores`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.get_stores)(\*[, root, images_store, ...])           | Build the lookbook Stores bundle.                                                                                     |
| [`ingest`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.ingest)(source)                                      | Materialize a source into a list of ImageRefs.                                                                        |
| [`to_local_path`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.to_local_path)(ref, \*[, cache_dir])                 | Return a filesystem path where the bytes of `ref` can be read.                                                        |
| [`score`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.score)(ref, \*, metric_id[, stores])                 | Score one image against one metric.                                                                                   |
| [`value_of`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.value_of)(manifest, image_id, metric_id[, ...])      | Return the bare value of an annotation (not the wrapper), or default.                                                 |

### *class* lookbook.IdentitySimilarity(metric_id='identity_similarity', cost_tier=2, requires=(), backend='lookbook:identity_similarity', reference_embedding=None, reference_image=None, reference_images=None, embedder='arcface', threshold=0.85, aggregation='max', normalization='rescale')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Score a candidate image’s identity-likeness to a locked reference.

Unlike the single-image scorers, this one is **stateful by reference**:
it holds the reference embedding(s) and compares each candidate against
them. Construct one per locked subject, then `score` every generation.

Construction (provide exactly one of the reference inputs):

- `reference_embedding` — a precomputed vector (1-D) or pool (2-D /
  sequence of vectors). Cheapest; the reference is never re-embedded.
- `reference_image` — a single [`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef) (or
  anything the injected embedder accepts), embedded **once** at
  construction and cached.
- `reference_images` — a pool of refs, each embedded once.

Parameters (keyword-only past the embedder seam):

- `embedder` — registry name (`"arcface"` default), an `Embedder`
  object, or a bare `embed_fn(ref) -> vector` callable. Injectable so
  tests pass a fake embedder and non-face subjects pass `"clip"` /
  `"dinov2"`.
- `threshold` — advisory pass/fail cutoff on the `[0, 1]` scale.
- `aggregation` — `"max"` (default) | `"mean"` | `"min"` over the
  reference pool.
- `normalization` — cosine → `[0, 1]` map; see `DFLT_NORMALIZATION`.

The `score(ref, manifest)` method returns a JSON-able dict (see
[`SimilarityResult.as_dict()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.SimilarityResult.as_dict)) so it persists through the manifest’s
default codec. Use [`compare_to_reference()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.compare_to_reference) for a one-call facade that
returns the typed [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.SimilarityResult).

#### compare(ref)

Compare one candidate ref against the reference; typed result.

* **Return type:**
  [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult)

#### *property* config_hash *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

changes whenever a setting that affects its output changes.

* **Type:**
  Cache key for this component

#### score(ref, manifest)

Scorer-protocol entry point — returns the JSON-able result dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

The aggregated **raw cosine** in `[-1, 1]` (pre-normalization). The
`identity_cosine` name is kept for the supervisor’s vocabulary even
when the embedder is CLIP/DINOv2 — it is the cosine in whatever space
the embedder defines.

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### score

The aggregated similarity normalized to `[0, 1]` (1 = same identity).
This is what the gate compares against `threshold`.

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### passed

`score >= threshold`. **Advisory only** — the consumer decides
whether to act on it.

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### threshold

The threshold used for `passed` (on the `[0, 1]` scale).

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### per_reference

The per-reference normalized similarities before aggregation. Length
is the size of the reference pool. Lets callers see *which* locked view
matched (e.g. `argmax` for `aggregation="max"`).

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

#### aggregation

The aggregation applied over `per_reference`.

* **Type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### n_references

Size of the reference pool.

* **Type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### as_dict()

JSON-able view (what the scorer writes to the manifest).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### *class* lookbook.Stores(images, manifest, runs, embeddings, root=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Bundle of all stores lookbook uses for persistence.

### lookbook.compare_to_reference(reference_image, candidate_image, , embedder='arcface', threshold=0.85, aggregation='max', normalization='rescale')

Compare a candidate to a reference in one call → [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.SimilarityResult).

The supervisor’s headline verb. `reference_image` may be a single image
ref or a **pool** (any sequence of refs) — the pool is embedded once and
folded by `aggregation`. `candidate_image` is a single ref.

All inputs are whatever the injected `embedder` accepts — typically an
[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef), but with a fake/callable embedder they
can be anything (tests pass plain ids).

* **Parameters:**
  * **embedder** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), Embedder, [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]) – Registry name (`"arcface"` default for faces; `"clip"` / `"dinov2"`
    for scenes/architecture), an `Embedder` object, or a bare
    `embed_fn(x) -> vector` callable.
  * **threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Advisory pass/fail cutoff on the `[0, 1]` scale (1 = same identity).
  * **aggregation** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – How to fold a reference pool — `"max"` (default), `"mean"`, `"min"`.
  * **normalization::** – Cosine → `[0, 1]` map — `"rescale"` (default) or `"clamp"`.
* **Returns:**
  `.score` (∈ `[0, 1]`), `.passed` (advisory), `.identity_cosine`
  (raw cosine), and the per-reference breakdown.
* **Return type:**
  [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult)

### lookbook.curate(source, , k=20, scorer_ids=('random_score',), embedder_ids=(), filter_ids=(), selector_id='top_k', diagnose_clusters=0, stores=None, constraints=None)

High-level facade: ingest a source, run a pipeline, return the result.

Each plugin id may be either a string (“blur”) or a (name, kwargs)
tuple ((“blur”, {“max_side”: 256})) to override the default config.

`diagnose_clusters > 0` runs cluster-coverage diagnosis after selection
and writes the result into the report’s `notes`.

* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)

### lookbook.curate_for_character(source, , k=1, face_detector='insightface', stores=None, constraints=None)

Curate the best reference image(s) of a *known* character from a pool.

Opinionated facade over [`curate()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate), tuned for the “pick the
reference image of this one character” job (IP-adapter conditioning,
model-sheet seeding): every image is scored for resolution, sharpness,
exposure and face quality, then the top `k` are taken by the
composite `face_quality` metric.

Identity is *not* scored — the pool is assumed to already be one
character, so what matters is which frame shows them most usably: in
focus, well exposed, face clearly visible and well sized. To check
whether a *generation* still matches a locked reference, use
[`lookbook.compare_to_reference()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.compare_to_reference) instead.

`face_detector` names the registered face-box scorer:

- `"insightface"` — real RetinaFace detection; needs
  `pip install lookbook[person]`. The default.
- `"mock_face"` — the deterministic centred-box detector, for tests
  and demos without the ML dependency.

Images with no detected face score `0` and sort last; the pool is
never filtered down to empty, so a small or awkward pool still yields
a best-effort pick.

* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)

### lookbook.curate_for_environment(source, , k=1, stores=None, constraints=None)

Curate the best reference image(s) for a non-person subject.

Opinionated facade over [`curate()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate) for pools where face detection
is moot — environment plates, prop references, style boards. Each
image is scored for resolution, sharpness and exposure, folded into
the composite `technical_quality` metric, and the top `k` are
taken.

Unlike [`curate_for_character()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate_for_character) this needs no ML dependency — the
scorers run on Pillow + numpy (cv2 is used for sharpness when present,
with a numpy fallback otherwise).

* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)

### lookbook.curate_interactive(source, , on_decision, k=20, present=8, max_rounds=20, scorer_ids=('random_score',), embedder_ids=(), filter_ids=(), selector_id='top_k', stores=None, constraints=None)

Run the pipeline in rounds, taking keep/reject decisions per round.

Args mirror [`lookbook.curate()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate) plus:

* **Parameters:**
  * **on_decision** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]], [`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision)]]) – A callable or a pre-recorded sequence of
    [`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.InteractiveDecision). The callable receives the
    round’s top candidates and an info dict
    `{round, n_kept_so_far, n_pool_remaining}`.
  * **present** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – How many candidates to surface per round.
  * **max_rounds** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Hard cap on iterations; a defensive guard against
    broken decision callables that never stop.
* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)
* **Returns:**
  A [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.RunResult) whose `kept` list is the confirmed
  set (in the order they were kept). `candidates` carries the
  same as the final round’s pre-selection candidate pool.

### lookbook.get_stores(, root=None, images_store=None, manifest_store=None, runs_store=None, embeddings=None)

Build the lookbook Stores bundle.

All arguments are optional. When `root` is None and no stores are

Materialize a source into a list of ImageRefs.

>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:

# _autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md

# lookbook.http

HTTP surface for lookbook, built with `qh` over FastAPI.

Each HTTP route is a thin function that takes JSON-able args and returns
a JSON-able dict. The route functions are the *only* thing this module
adds — all real work is delegated to the existing facade.

Build the app with `mk_lookbook_app()` and run it with `serve()` (or use
the `lookbook serve` CLI command).

### Functions

| [`compare_to_reference`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.compare_to_reference)(\*, reference_paths, ...)   | Identity/likeness of a candidate vs a locked reference (or pool).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`curate_source`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.curate_source)(source_path, \*[, k, recipe])      | Run a recipe on a directory of images.                              |
| [`get_annotations`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.get_annotations)(image_id)                        | All annotations for one image (drawn from the manifest).            |
| [`get_image`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.get_image)(image_id)                              | Return the raw bytes of an image by id.                             |
| [`get_run`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.get_run)(run_id)                                  | One run record by id.                                               |
| [`ingest_source`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.ingest_source)(source_path)                       | Ingest a directory or file.                                         |
| [`list_plugins`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.list_plugins)()                                   | All registered scorers / embedders / filters / selectors.           |
| [`list_recipes`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.list_recipes)()                                   | All available recipes / profiles, with their specs.                 |
| [`list_runs`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.list_runs)()                                      | All run ids stored on the server.                                   |
| [`mk_lookbook_app`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.mk_lookbook_app)(\*[, app])                       | Build a FastAPI app exposing the lookbook HTTP surface.             |
| [`reset_stores`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.reset_stores)([stores])                           | Replace the server-wide stores.                                     |
| [`score_image`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.score_image)(\*[, source_path, image_id])         | Score a single image by metric id.                                  |
| [`serve`](_autosummary/lookbook.http.html.md#lookbook.http.serve)(\*[, host, port])                          | Run the lookbook HTTP server (uvicorn under the hood).              |

### lookbook.http.compare_to_reference(, reference_paths, candidate_path, embedder='arcface', threshold=0.85, aggregation='max', normalization='rescale')

Identity/likeness of a candidate vs a locked reference (or pool).

The reference-supervisor verb: returns a normalized similarity in
`[0, 1]` (1 = same identity) plus an advisory `passed` flag. Pass one
or more `reference_paths` (server-local image paths) and a single
`candidate_path`. `embedder` selects the space — `"arcface"` for
faces (default), `"clip"` / `"dinov2"` for scenes/architecture.

The pass/fail is **advisory** — the caller decides whether to act on it.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.curate_source(source_path, , k=20, recipe='funnel')

Run a recipe on a directory of images. Returns the run record.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.get_annotations(image_id)

All annotations for one image (drawn from the manifest).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.get_image(image_id)

Return the raw bytes of an image by id.

The server reads from `stores.images[image_id]["path"]`. If the entry
is missing, returns a 404-style error dict (FastAPI surfaces this as a
JSON response; a future iteration may switch to a streaming binary
response via FastAPI’s `Response`).

### lookbook.http.get_run(run_id)

One run record by id.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.ingest_source(source_path)

Ingest a directory or file. Records id->path in `stores.images`.

Returns the list of resolved image ids.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.list_plugins()

All registered scorers / embedders / filters / selectors.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.list_recipes()

All available recipes / profiles, with their specs.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.list_runs()

All run ids stored on the server.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.mk_lookbook_app(, app=None, \*\*kwargs)

Build a FastAPI app exposing the lookbook HTTP surface.

Each function becomes a POST endpoint with a JSON body matching its
keyword arguments. Use the auto-generated `/docs` (Swagger) or
`/redoc` for interactive exploration. Disabling qh’s convention-based
routing keeps the path scheme uniform — every route is `POST /<verb>`
and takes a JSON body — which is the pattern most agent clients
(and our future MCP layer) expect.

### lookbook.http.reset_stores(stores=None)

Replace the server-wide stores. Used by tests; rare otherwise.

### lookbook.http.score_image(, source_path='', image_id='', metric_id)

Score a single image by metric id.

Pass either `source_path` (file path on the server) or `image_id`
(must already have a path recorded via ingest).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.http.serve(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8000, \*\*kwargs)

Run the lookbook HTTP server (uvicorn under the hood).


# _autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md

# lookbook.interactive

Interactive curate loop — keep the human in the loop.

The non-interactive [`lookbook.curate()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate) runs the pipeline once
and returns its top-k. That works for fully-automated workflows but
loses the human’s taste signal: a ranking that ranks “boring but
high-quality” images above “stylistically perfect but slightly
blurry” ones.

[`curate_interactive()`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.curate_interactive) invites the caller into the loop. Each
round:

1. The pipeline picks the top `present` unseen candidates.
2. The caller’s `on_decision(refs, info)` returns an
   [`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision) saying which to keep, which to
   > reject, and whether to stop.
3. Kept refs lock into the final selection. Rejected refs leave the
   candidate pool and won’t be shown again. Everything else is
   eligible to come back next round (handy when the caller wants to
   defer a decision).
4. The loop terminates when the caller says `stop`, when the
   confirmed-kept set reaches `k`, when the candidate pool is
   exhausted, or when `max_rounds` is reached.

Two `on_decision` shapes are supported:

- A function: `on_decision(refs, info) -> InteractiveDecision`.
- A list of pre-recorded [`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision) items, applied
  one per round. Useful for tests and headless replays.

### Functions

| [`curate_interactive`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.curate_interactive)(source, \*, on_decision[, ...])   | Run the pipeline in rounds, taking keep/reject decisions per round.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision)(\*[, keep, reject, stop])   | One round's verdict from the caller.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|

### *class* lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision(, keep=(), reject=(), stop=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One round’s verdict from the caller.

#### keep

```
``
```

image_id\`\`s the caller wants to lock into the final
selection. They’re added immediately, removed from the
candidate pool, and not shown again.

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

#### reject

```
``
```

image_id\`\`s the caller never wants to see again in
this run.

* **Type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

#### stop

When True, the loop terminates after applying this
round’s keep/reject and returns whatever is in the
confirmed-kept set so far (clipped to `k`).

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### lookbook.interactive.curate_interactive(source, , on_decision, k=20, present=8, max_rounds=20, scorer_ids=('random_score',), embedder_ids=(), filter_ids=(), selector_id='top_k', stores=None, constraints=None)

Run the pipeline in rounds, taking keep/reject decisions per round.

Args mirror [`lookbook.curate()`](_autosummary/lookbook.html.md#lookbook.curate) plus:

* **Parameters:**
  * **on_decision** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]], [`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision)]]) – A callable or a pre-recorded sequence of
    [`InteractiveDecision`](_autosummary/lookbook.interactive.html.md#lookbook.interactive.InteractiveDecision). The callable receives the
    round’s top candidates and an info dict
    `{round, n_kept_so_far, n_pool_remaining}`.
  * **present** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – How many candidates to surface per round.
  * **max_rounds** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Hard cap on iterations; a defensive guard against
    broken decision callables that never stop.
* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)
* **Returns:**
  A `RunResult` whose `kept` list is the confirmed
  set (in the order they were kept). `candidates` carries the
  same as the final round’s pre-selection candidate pool.

# _autosummary/lookbook.io.ingest.html.md

# lookbook.io.ingest

### lookbook.io.ingest(source)

Materialize a source into a list of ImageRefs.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     for name in ['a.jpg', 'b.png', 'note.txt']:
...         open(os.path.join(d, name), 'wb').close()
...     refs = ingest(d)
>>> sorted(os.path.basename(r.path) for r in refs)
['a.jpg', 'b.png']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef)]

# _autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md

# lookbook.mcp

MCP surface for lookbook, built with `fastmcp`.

Each verb from `lookbook.http` is exposed as an MCP tool that an LLM
agent can call. The tool functions are intentionally the same callables
used by the HTTP layer — JSON-able args, JSON-able returns. This means
swapping between an HTTP frontend and an MCP frontend is “wire it once,
expose it twice.”

Run the server over stdio with `lookbook mcp` (the default transport
that Claude Desktop and the Anthropic SDK expect).

### Functions

| [`mcp_compare_to_reference`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_compare_to_reference)(reference_paths, ...)   | Check whether a generated image still matches a locked reference.    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`mcp_curate_source`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_curate_source)(source_path[, k, recipe])      | Run a full curation pipeline on a directory and return the K best.   |
| [`mcp_get_annotations`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_get_annotations)(image_id)                    | All annotations stored for one image.                                |
| [`mcp_get_image`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_get_image)(image_id)                          | Look up an image's path and metadata by id.                          |
| [`mcp_get_run`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_get_run)(run_id)                              | Fetch a stored run record by id.                                     |
| [`mcp_ingest_source`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_ingest_source)(source_path)                   | Scan a directory or file for images and register them on the server. |
| [`mcp_list_plugins`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_list_plugins)()                               | List every registered scorer / embedder / filter / selector.         |
| [`mcp_list_recipes`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_list_recipes)()                               | List every available curation recipe / profile.                      |
| [`mcp_list_runs`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_list_runs)()                                  | All curation runs stored on this server.                             |
| [`mcp_score_image`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mcp_score_image)(metric_id[, source_path, ...])   | Score one image against one metric and cache the result.             |
| [`mk_lookbook_mcp`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.mk_lookbook_mcp)(\*[, name])                      | Build a FastMCP server exposing the lookbook curation verbs.         |
| [`serve`](_autosummary/lookbook.mcp.html.md#lookbook.mcp.serve)(\*[, transport])                           | Run the lookbook MCP server.                                         |

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_compare_to_reference(reference_paths, candidate_path, embedder='arcface', threshold=0.85, aggregation='max', normalization='rescale')

Check whether a generated image still matches a locked reference.

The reference-supervisor verb. Embeds the candidate and the reference(s)
in the chosen space and returns a normalized identity similarity in
`[0, 1]` (1 = same identity) plus an advisory `passed` flag against the
threshold. The pass/fail is advisory — you decide whether to act on it.

* **Parameters:**
  * **reference_paths** ([`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)) – one or more server-local paths of the locked
    reference image(s). A pool is folded by `aggregation`.
  * **candidate_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – server-local path of the candidate generation.
  * **embedder** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"arcface"` for face identity (default), `"clip"` or
    `"dinov2"` for scenes / architecture / props.
  * **threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – advisory pass/fail cutoff on the [0, 1] scale.
  * **aggregation** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – how to fold a reference pool — `"max"` (matches any
    locked view; default), `"mean"`, or `"min"`.
  * **normalization** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – cosine→[0,1] map — `"rescale"` (default) or `"clamp"`.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)
* **Returns:**
  ```
  `
  ```

  {identity_cosine, score, passed, threshold, per_reference,
  : aggregation, n_references}\`.

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_curate_source(source_path, k=20, recipe='funnel')

Run a full curation pipeline on a directory and return the K best.

The high-level entry point. Picks K reference images from the
directory using the named recipe (cheap funnel, embeddings + facility
location, person profile, etc.). Returns a run record containing the
chosen image_ids, drop attributions per filter, optional cluster
coverage, scorer ids that ran, and run timing.

* **Parameters:**
  * **source_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – absolute path to the directory of candidate images.
  * **k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – target subset size (the number of images to keep).
  * **recipe** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a recipe / profile name. Use `list_recipes` to see options.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Common recipes:

> - `random`        : placeholder, deterministic, no real scoring.
> - `funnel`        : Phase 1 cheap filter — fast, no GPU.
> - `funnel_relaxed`: same but lower thresholds for typical phone shots.
> - `diverse`       : DINOv2 embeddings + facility-location.
> - `diverse_clip`  : same with CLIP semantic embeddings.
> - `person`
>   : ArcFace identity + pose-bin quotas).
> - `person_mock`   : person without model downloads (testing).

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_get_annotations(image_id)

All annotations stored for one image.

Includes the metric_id, value, config_hash, cost_tier, backend, and
timestamp for each annotation. Use this to understand *why* an image
was kept or rejected — the manifest holds the full provenance.

* **Parameters:**
  **image_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – as returned from `ingest_source` or `curate_source`.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_get_image(image_id)

Look up an image’s path and metadata by id.

Returns `{image_id, path, n_bytes}` when found. Phase 5 returns
metadata only — agents that want the raw bytes should read the file
directly when running on the same host as the server.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_get_run(run_id)

Fetch a stored run record by id.

The run record contains: kept and candidate image_ids, scorer_ids,
selector_id, started_at / finished_at timestamps, and a `report`
block with drop attributions and (when applicable) cluster coverage.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_ingest_source(source_path)

Scan a directory or file for images and register them on the server.

Records `image_id -> path` in the server’s image store so later calls
(`score_image`, `get_image`, `curate_source`) can refer to images by
id. Returns the list of image_ids and the count.

* **Parameters:**
  **source_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – absolute path on the server’s filesystem.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_list_plugins()

List every registered scorer / embedder / filter / selector.

Use this to discover available metric_ids for `score_image` and to
understand what capabilities each recipe is wiring together.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_list_recipes()

List every available curation recipe / profile.

Returns a dict where each value is a recipe spec describing the
scorers, embedders, filters, selector, and default constraints. Use
this first to see what `curate_source` will accept for the `recipe`
argument.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_list_runs()

All curation runs stored on this server.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mcp_score_image(metric_id, source_path='', image_id='')

Score one image against one metric and cache the result.

Pass either `source_path` (a path on the server) or `image_id` (must
already be registered via `ingest_source`). Returns the metric value;
re-running with the same metric_id and config is free.

* **Parameters:**
  * **metric_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a registered scorer name (see `list_plugins`).
  * **source_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – optional, the path to the image.
  * **image_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – optional, an id from a previous `ingest_source`.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.mcp.mk_lookbook_mcp(, name='lookbook')

Build a FastMCP server exposing the lookbook curation verbs.

Each verb becomes an MCP tool. The agent’s typical sequence is:

> list_recipes() -> pick a recipe
> curate_source(path, k, recipe) -> get back a run record
> get_annotations(image_id) -> understand why each kept image won
> get_run(run_id) -> review the full report

The server uses the same Stores singleton as `lookbook.http`, so an
HTTP server and an MCP server backed by the same data folder share
the manifest and the runs index.

### lookbook.mcp.serve(, transport='stdio', \*\*kwargs)

Run the lookbook MCP server.

The default transport is stdio — the protocol Claude Desktop and the
Anthropic SDK expect when launching an MCP server as a subprocess.
Pass `transport="http"` (and a port via kwargs) for HTTP-streamable
transport.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md

# lookbook.pipeline

Pipeline orchestrator.

A `Pipeline` is a list of scorers (and, later, filters/embedders) plus a
final selector. Running it:

1. Topologically orders the scorers by their `requires` declarations.
2. Walks them in cost-tier order, writing results to the manifest.
3. Hands the surviving candidates plus the read-only manifest to the
   selector.

The orchestration is a hand-rolled topo walk. Swapping in `meshed.DAG` for
richer dependency graphs and caching was planned but never taken up; nothing
in the package imports `meshed`. Whoever does make that switch: the
`Scorer.requires` field is already the dependency graph.

### Classes

| [`Pipeline`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.Pipeline)([scorers, embedders, filters, ...])    | An ordered set of scorers + embedders + filters + a final selector.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)(run_id, kept, candidates, ...[, ...]) | The result of running a pipeline.                                     |

`stores` defaults to in-memory. Pass `get_stores()` for the user’s

* **Return type:**
  [`RunResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.pipeline.html.md#lookbook.pipeline.RunResult)

# _autosummary/lookbook.profiles.html.md

# lookbook.profiles

Subject profiles — declarative recipes loaded from YAML.

A profile is just a recipe with a name and a YAML file. The schema mirrors
the in-code `RECIPES` dict in `lookbook/__main__.py`:

> name: person
> description: short description shown in `lookbook list-recipes`
> scorers: [scorer_id, …]
> embedders: [embedder_id, …]   # optional
> filters: [filter_id, …]       # may include [name, kwargs] entries
> selector: selector_id           # may be [name, kwargs]
> diagnose_clusters: 12           # optional
> constraints: { … }            # default constraints (e.g. quotas)

Profiles ship in `lookbook/profiles/*.yaml`. Users can override or add
profiles by dropping YAML files into `<config_root>/profiles/` (resolved
via `config2py`).

### Functions

| [`list_profiles`](_autosummary/lookbook.profiles.html.md#lookbook.profiles.list_profiles)()   | All profile names available, shipped + user-defined.    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| [`load`](_autosummary/lookbook.profiles.html.md#lookbook.profiles.load)(name)        | Load a profile by name, returning a recipe-shaped dict. |

### lookbook.profiles.list_profiles()

All profile names available, shipped + user-defined.

User profiles override shipped ones with the same name.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### lookbook.profiles.load(name)

Load a profile by name, returning a recipe-shaped dict.

Raises `KeyError` if the profile is unknown.

```pycon
>>> spec = load("person")
>>> "scorers" in spec
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/lookbook.refs.html.md

# lookbook.refs

Concrete `ImageRef` implementations.

Refs are the unit of identity in lookbook. The orchestrator passes refs
around; scorers open them lazily; the manifest is keyed by `image_id`.

Three impls are provided here. None of them require Pillow at import time;
`open()` defers the import.

All three expose `local_path(cache_dir=None) -> str` — a path on the
local filesystem that the bytes are reachable through. Path refs return
their existing path; bytes/url refs materialize once into a content-
addressed cache and reuse the result. This is the ergonomic surface for
downstream tools that want a file (e.g. ffmpeg, lookbook → fal upload).

### Functions

| [`to_local_path`](_autosummary/lookbook.refs.html.md#lookbook.refs.to_local_path)(ref, \*[, cache_dir])   | Return a filesystem path where the bytes of `ref` can be read.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`BytesImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.refs.html.md#lookbook.refs.BytesImageRef)(payload[, image_id, metadata])     | An image stored as raw bytes in memory.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| [`PathImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.refs.html.md#lookbook.refs.PathImageRef)(path[, image_id, metadata])         | An image referenced by filesystem path.   |
| [`UrlImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.refs.html.md#lookbook.refs.UrlImageRef)(url[, image_id, metadata, \_cached]) | An image referenced by URL.               |

  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# lookbook.registry

Plugin registry for scorers, filters, embedders, selectors.

Anything that implements one of the protocols in `lookbook.base` can be

# _autosummary/lookbook.report.html.md

# lookbook.report

Run report — what happened during a curation pass.

The report is the user-facing artifact alongside the kept set. It explains
*why* images were dropped and what the kept set looks like, in terms a
human (or an LLM agent) can act on.

Phase 1 ships the drop-attribution part. Coverage / set-level diagnosis
lands in Phase 2 alongside embeddings.

### Functions

| [`attribute_drops`](_autosummary/lookbook.report.html.md#lookbook.report.attribute_drops)(candidates, filters, manifest)   | Apply filters in order, attributing each drop to the first filter that rejected it.   |

Scorers: per-image annotation producers.

Each submodule registers its scorers into `lookbook.registry.scorers` on
import. Heavy ML deps must be lazy-imported inside scorer methods, never at
module top.
