# _autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md

# lookbook.scorers.identity

Cross-image identity / likeness scorer — compare a candidate to a reference.

Every scorer in [`lookbook.scorers`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.html.md#module-lookbook.scorers) rates a *single* image’s technical or
face quality. This module adds the missing primitive: a scorer that **compares**
a candidate image against a locked **reference** (or a pool of references) and
returns an identity-similarity number in `[0, 1]` (1 = same identity).

This is the measurement substrate for a “reference supervisor” — answering
 *“does this generation still match the locked reference?”* with a number a
caller can gate on. It reuses lookbook’s existing embedders unchanged:

- `arcface` (InsightFace `buffalo_l`) for **face identity** — the default;
  neither CLIP nor DINOv2 reliably says “same person”.
- `clip` / `dinov2` for **non-face subjects** (locations, architecture,
  props) — injected via the same `embedder=` seam.

## Design notes

- **The embedder is injected, never hard-wired.** [`IdentitySimilarity`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.IdentitySimilarity)
  accepts an [`Embedder`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.Embedder), a registry name (resolved
  lazily), or a bare `embed_fn(ref) -> vector` callable. This keeps the heavy
  ML deps (torch / insightface) behind lookbook’s usual lazy boundary —
  importing this module pulls in nothing heavy — and makes the cosine math
  unit-testable with a fake embedder returning known vectors.
- **The reference is embedded once.** Pass a precomputed `reference_embedding`
  (a single vector or a stacked array of vectors for a pool), or a reference
  image / list of images that the scorer embeds **once at construction** and
  caches. Candidates are never made to pay for re-embedding the reference.
- **Set aggregation** is explicit: when the reference is a pool, the per-view
  similarities are aggregated by `aggregation` (default `"max"` — “matches
  *any* locked view”, the right default for a supervisor; `"mean"` is the
  stricter “matches the *average* view”).
- The result carries a `passed` flag against an injectable `threshold`.
  This is **advisory** — the consumer (e.g. reelee’s reference supervisor)
  decides whether to hard-block. Nothing here raises on a low score.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_THRESHOLD`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_THRESHOLD)     | Default normalized-similarity threshold for the advisory pass/fail gate.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_EMBEDDER`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_EMBEDDER)      | Default embedder used when none is injected.                               |
| [`DFLT_AGGREGATION`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_AGGREGATION)   | How to fold a pool of per-reference similarities into one number.          |
| [`DFLT_NORMALIZATION`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_NORMALIZATION) | How to map a cosine in `[-1, 1]` onto `[0, 1]`.                            |
| [`METRIC_ID`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.METRIC_ID)          | The metric_id this scorer writes to the manifest.                          |

### Functions

| [`compare_to_reference`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.compare_to_reference)(reference_image, ...[, ...])   | Compare a candidate to a reference in one call → [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`cosine_similarity`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.cosine_similarity)(u, v)                             | Cosine similarity in `[-1, 1]` between two vectors.                                                                   |
| [`normalize_cosine`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.normalize_cosine)(cosine, \*[, normalization])       | Map a cosine in `[-1, 1]` onto `[0, 1]` (1 = identical direction).                                                    |

### Classes

| [`IdentitySimilarity`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.IdentitySimilarity)([metric_id, cost_tier, ...])   | Score a candidate image's identity-likeness to a locked reference.      |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult)(identity_cosine, score, ...)     | Outcome of comparing a candidate against a (possibly pooled) reference. |

### lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_AGGREGATION *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= 'max'*

How to fold a pool of per-reference similarities into one number.

### lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_EMBEDDER *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= 'arcface'*

Default embedder used when none is injected. `"arcface"` is the identity
space; swap for `"clip"` / `"dinov2"` for non-face subjects.

### lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_NORMALIZATION *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= 'rescale'*

How to map a cosine in `[-1, 1]` onto `[0, 1]`.

- `"rescale"`: `(cos + 1) / 2` — order-preserving over the full range;
  the safe default for any embedder (CLIP/DINOv2 cosines can go negative).
- `"clamp"`: `max(0, cos)` — for L2-normalized identity spaces where a
  negative cosine just means “unrelated” and should floor at 0.

### lookbook.scorers.identity.DFLT_THRESHOLD *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* *= 0.85*

Default normalized-similarity threshold for the advisory pass/fail gate.
On the `[0, 1]` scale (1 = same identity). 0.85 mirrors the common
ArcFace “same person” operating point; owner-tunable per call.

### *class* lookbook.scorers.identity.IdentitySimilarity(metric_id='identity_similarity', cost_tier=2, requires=(), backend='lookbook:identity_similarity', reference_embedding=None, reference_image=None, reference_images=None, embedder='arcface', threshold=0.85, aggregation='max', normalization='rescale')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Score a candidate image’s identity-likeness to a locked reference.

Unlike the single-image scorers, this one is **stateful by reference**:
it holds the reference embedding(s) and compares each candidate against
them. Construct one per locked subject, then `score` every generation.

Construction (provide exactly one of the reference inputs):

- `reference_embedding` — a precomputed vector (1-D) or pool (2-D /
  sequence of vectors). Cheapest; the reference is never re-embedded.
- `reference_image` — a single [`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef) (or
  anything the injected embedder accepts), embedded **once** at
  construction and cached.
- `reference_images` — a pool of refs, each embedded once.

Parameters (keyword-only past the embedder seam):

- `embedder` — registry name (`"arcface"` default), an `Embedder`
  object, or a bare `embed_fn(ref) -> vector` callable. Injectable so
  tests pass a fake embedder and non-face subjects pass `"clip"` /
  `"dinov2"`.
- `threshold` — advisory pass/fail cutoff on the `[0, 1]` scale.
- `aggregation` — `"max"` (default) | `"mean"` | `"min"` over the
  reference pool.
- `normalization` — cosine → `[0, 1]` map; see `DFLT_NORMALIZATION`.

The `score(ref, manifest)` method returns a JSON-able dict (see
[`SimilarityResult.as_dict()`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult.as_dict)) so it persists through the manifest’s
default codec. Use [`compare_to_reference()`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.compare_to_reference) for a one-call facade that
returns the typed [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult).

#### compare(ref)

Compare one candidate ref against the reference; typed result.

* **Return type:**
  [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult)

changes whenever a setting that affects its output changes.

  Cache key for this component

#### score(ref, manifest)

Scorer-protocol entry point — returns the JSON-able result dict.

  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### lookbook.scorers.identity.METRIC_ID *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= 'identity_similarity'*

The metric_id this scorer writes to the manifest.

### *class* lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult(identity_cosine, score, passed, threshold, per_reference=tuple(), aggregation='max', n_references=0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Outcome of comparing a candidate against a (possibly pooled) reference.

### lookbook.scorers.identity.compare_to_reference(reference_image, candidate_image, , embedder='arcface', threshold=0.85, aggregation='max', normalization='rescale')

Compare a candidate to a reference in one call → [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult).

The supervisor’s headline verb. `reference_image` may be a single image
ref or a **pool** (any sequence of refs) — the pool is embedded once and
folded by `aggregation`. `candidate_image` is a single ref.

All inputs are whatever the injected `embedder` accepts — typically an
[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef), but with a fake/callable embedder they
can be anything (tests pass plain ids).

* **Parameters:**
  * **embedder** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), Embedder, [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]) – Registry name (`"arcface"` default for faces; `"clip"` / `"dinov2"`
    for scenes/architecture), an `Embedder` object, or a bare
    `embed_fn(x) -> vector` callable.
  * **threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Advisory pass/fail cutoff on the `[0, 1]` scale (1 = same identity).
  * **aggregation** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – How to fold a reference pool — `"max"` (default), `"mean"`, `"min"`.
  * **normalization::** – Cosine → `[0, 1]` map — `"rescale"` (default) or `"clamp"`.
* **Returns:**
  `.score` (∈ `[0, 1]`), `.passed` (advisory), `.identity_cosine`
  (raw cosine), and the per-reference breakdown.
* **Return type:**
  [`SimilarityResult`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.identity.html.md#lookbook.scorers.identity.SimilarityResult)

### lookbook.scorers.identity.cosine_similarity(u, v)

Cosine similarity in `[-1, 1]` between two vectors.

Safe against unnormalized inputs and zero vectors (returns 0.0 when either
has zero magnitude, which is what a no-face ArcFace embedding yields).

```pycon
>>> cosine_similarity(np.array([1.0, 0.0]), np.array([1.0, 0.0]))
1.0
>>> cosine_similarity(np.array([1.0, 0.0]), np.array([-1.0, 0.0]))
-1.0
>>> cosine_similarity(np.array([1.0, 0.0]), np.array([0.0, 1.0]))
0.0
>>> cosine_similarity(np.array([0.0, 0.0]), np.array([1.0, 0.0]))
0.0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### lookbook.scorers.identity.normalize_cosine(cosine, , normalization='rescale')

Map a cosine in `[-1, 1]` onto `[0, 1]` (1 = identical direction).

```pycon
>>> normalize_cosine(1.0)
1.0
>>> normalize_cosine(-1.0)
0.0
>>> normalize_cosine(0.0)
0.5
>>> normalize_cosine(-0.3, normalization="clamp")
0.0
>>> normalize_cosine(0.6, normalization="clamp")
0.6
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/lookbook.scorers.person.html.md

# lookbook.scorers.person

Person-LoRA scorers — Phase 3.

Two backends ship for face detection:

- `MockFaceDetect`: synthesizes a centered face box, deterministic, no deps.
  Used by tests and by users who already have face boxes from another tool.
- `InsightFaceDetect`: real RetinaFace + landmarks + (optionally) gender/age,
  lazy-imported. Use for production.

Both write to the same `face_box` metric_id. They are distinguished by
`config_hash` so the cache invalidates if the user swaps backends.

Downstream scorers (`FaceArea`, `HeadPose`, `FaceQualityProxy`) read
`face_box` from the manifest via the `requires` mechanism. They never touch
the detector directly — the orchestrator runs the detector first.

The value shape of `face_box` (when a face is detected):

> {
> : “x1”: int, “y1”: int, “x2”: int, “y2”: int,
>   “confidence”: float,         # detector score
>   “n_faces”: int,              # total faces detected before keeping the largest
>   “landmarks”: list | None,    # 5 (x, y) pairs if available, else None

> }

When no face is detected, the value is `None`.

### Classes

| [`FaceArea`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.person.html.md#lookbook.scorers.person.FaceArea)([metric_id, cost_tier, requires, ...])   | Face area as a fraction of total image area, plus a size bin.                           |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`FaceQualityProxy`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.person.html.md#lookbook.scorers.person.FaceQualityProxy)([metric_id, cost_tier, ...])     | Combine detector confidence, face area, and (optionally) blur into a single 0..1 score. |
| [`InsightFaceDetect`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.person.html.md#lookbook.scorers.person.InsightFaceDetect)([metric_id, cost_tier, ...])    | RetinaFace face detection via insightface.                                              |
| [`MockFaceDetect`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.person.html.md#lookbook.scorers.person.MockFaceDetect)([metric_id, cost_tier, ...])       | Deterministic face detector — synthesizes one centered box per image.                   |
| [`MockHeadPose`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.person.html.md#lookbook.scorers.person.MockHeadPose)([metric_id, cost_tier, ...])         | Synthetic head pose — deterministic from image_id.                                      |
| [`SixDRepNetHeadPose`](_autosummary/lookbook.scorers.person.html.md#lookbook.scorers.person.SixDRepNetHeadPose)([metric_id, cost_tier, ...])   | Head-pose estimation via 6DRepNet (lazy-imported).                                      |

# _autosummary/lookbook.scorers.technical.html.md

# lookbook.scorers.technical

Technical scorers — Phase 0/1.

Phase 0 ships `RandomScore` (placeholder for end-to-end orchestration).

Phase 1 adds the cheap-funnel scorers — these run on CPU with Pillow + numpy
as the base path, falling back to richer backends (cv2, imagehash) when
they’re available. None of them require torch or any GPU dep.

metric_id     | tier | requires    | needs                |
<br/>

```
|---------------|
```

——

```
|-------------|
```

———————-|
| resolution    | T0   | —           | Pillow               |
| file_hash     | T0   | —           | stdlib               |
| phash         | T1   | —           | imagehash (optional) |
| blur          | T1   | —           | numpy (cv2 optional) |
| exposure      | T1   | —           | numpy + Pillow       |

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Composite 0..1 technical-quality score. T1, derived.

Reads `blur`, `exposure`, and `resolution` from the manifest (the
orchestrator’s topo-sort runs them first via `requires`) and folds
them into one rankable number. This is the non-face counterpart of
`face_quality`: it gives `top_k` a single metric for curating image
pools where no face is involved — environment plates, prop refs,
style boards.

The blend is sharpness-dominant (a soft or blown reference is the
worst failure mode), with exposure clipping and resolution as
secondary terms. `blur` missing yields a neutral 0.5 sharpness so a
pool scored without the blur scorer still ranks by exposure + size.

changes whenever a setting that affects its output changes.

# _autosummary/lookbook.selectors.quota.html.md

# lookbook.selectors.quota

Quota-aware selection: pick K from N with per-bin budgets.

The QuotaSelector wraps an inner selector and runs it once per bin. Bins
are derived from a manifest annotation (`bin_metric_id`); quotas are a
mapping from bin label to a count.

Typical use for character LoRAs:

> QuotaSelector(
> : bin_metric_id=”head_pose.yaw_bin”,   # or any nested-key path
>   inner_selector_id=”top_k”,
>   inner_overrides={“metric_id”: “face_quality”},

> )

> # via curate(…)
> constraints = {“quotas”: {“front”: 8, “three_quarter”: 5, “profile”: 3, “back”: 1}}

If a bin doesn’t reach its quota (not enough survivors there), the deficit
falls back to the highest-quality survivors from any bin so the kept-set
size still hits K when possible. Set `strict=True` to disable that fallback.

### Classes

| [`QuotaSelector`](_autosummary/lookbook.selectors.quota.html.md#lookbook.selectors.quota.QuotaSelector)([selector_id, bin_metric_id, ...])   | Per-bin quota selection wrapping an inner Selector.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* lookbook.selectors.quota.QuotaSelector(selector_id='quota', bin_metric_id='head_pose.yaw_bin', inner_selector_id='top_k', inner_overrides=dict(), strict=False, embedding_space=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

# _autosummary/lookbook.selectors.submodular.html.md

# lookbook.selectors.submodular

Submodular selectors over embedding spaces.

Phase 2 ships a greedy facility-location selector implemented in pure
numpy. It’s the right default for “best K from N” when diversity matters:

> f(S) = sum over y in V of max over x in S of similarity(x, y)

> > + alpha \* sum over x in S of quality(x)

The greedy algorithm gives a (1 - 1/e) ≈ 0.63 approximation guarantee.
For typical curation sizes (N ≤ 1000, K ≤ 50), pure numpy is fast enough
and avoids the `apricot` dependency. For larger pools, swap in `apricot`’s
optimized lazy-greedy via the same Selector protocol.

Embeddings are not read from the manifest directly. The pipeline pre-fetches
them from `stores.embeddings[space_id]` and passes them via
`constraints["embeddings"]` as a `dict[image_id, np.ndarray]`.

### Classes

| [`FacilityLocation`](_autosummary/lookbook.selectors.submodular.html.md#lookbook.selectors.submodular.FacilityLocation)([selector_id, ...])   | Greedy facility-location subset selection.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|

### *class* lookbook.selectors.submodular.FacilityLocation(selector_id='facility_location', embedding_space='dinov2_base', quality_metric_id='', weight_quality=0.0, weight_diversity=1.0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Greedy facility-location subset selection.

The objective is:

```default
f(S) = sum_y max_{x in S} sim(x, y)  +  weight_quality * sum_{x in S} q(x)
```

where `sim` is cosine similarity (assumes embeddings are L2-normalized;
if they are not, the selector normalizes them first) and `q(x)` is the
annotation `quality_metric_id` for `x`, defaulting to 0 when absent.

`weight_quality=0` gives a pure-diversity selection. `weight_quality`
in 0.1–0.5 typically works well for “diverse but high-quality.”

#### select(candidates, manifest, k, constraints=None)

Choose the images to keep from the scored candidates.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ImageRef`](_autosummary/lookbook.base.html.md#lookbook.base.ImageRef)]

# _autosummary/lookbook.store.html.md

# lookbook.store

Repository pattern for lookbook persistence.

Three stores hold the package’s state. All three are MutableMappings so the
backend (filesystem, SQLite, S3, Mongo, in-memory) is swappable:

- `images`: image_id -> record about the image, e.g. `{"path": ...}`
- `manifest`: “image_id–metric_id” -> Annotation (as dict via codec)
- `runs`: run_id -> run record (recipe, kept set, report)

The default factory wires everything to JSON-on-disk under the user’s app
data folder (via config2py). Tests pass `dict()` everywhere to skip I/O.

### Functions

| [`get_stores`](_autosummary/lookbook.store.html.md#lookbook.store.get_stores)(\*[, root, images_store, ...])   | Build the lookbook Stores bundle.                             |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`manifest_codec`](_autosummary/lookbook.store.html.md#lookbook.store.manifest_codec)(store)                       | Wrap a string-keyed JSON-dict store so it speaks Annotations. |

### Classes

| [`Stores`](_autosummary/lookbook.store.html.md#lookbook.store.Stores)(images, manifest, runs, embeddings[, ...])   | Bundle of all stores lookbook uses for persistence.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* lookbook.store.Stores(images, manifest, runs, embeddings, root=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Bundle of all stores lookbook uses for persistence.

### lookbook.store.get_stores(, root=None, images_store=None, manifest_store=None, runs_store=None, embeddings=None)

Build the lookbook Stores bundle.

All arguments are optional. When `root` is None and no stores are
supplied, the user’s app data folder is used. Pass `dict()` for any
slot to keep that store in memory (useful for tests).

```pycon
>>> stores = get_stores(
...     images_store={}, manifest_store={}, runs_store={}, embeddings={}
... )
>>> stores.manifest is not None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Stores`](_autosummary/lookbook.store.html.md#lookbook.store.Stores)

### lookbook.store.manifest_codec(store)

Wrap a string-keyed JSON-dict store so it speaks Annotations.

Keys flow as `(image_id, metric_id) <-> "image_id--metric_id.json"`.
Values flow as `Annotation <-> dict`.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

# For AI agents

`lookbook` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `lookbook-add-scorer`

Use when adding a new per-image metric (scorer) to lookbook — wrapping a model from pyiqa/insightface/CLIP, adding technical metrics like noise or compression detection, or any “score one image” annotation producer. Triggers on “add a scorer”, “wrap pyiqa model X”, “add a metric for Y”, “score images by Z”.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-add-scorer`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-add-scorer).

### `lookbook-add-selector`

Use when adding a new selector to lookbook — wrapping an apricot submodular function, building a quota/constraint selector, integrating DPPy, or implementing a custom set-selection algorithm. Triggers on “add a selector”, “wrap a submodular function”, “quota-aware selection”, “DPP selector”, “custom set selection”.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-add-selector`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-add-selector).

### `lookbook-curate`

Use when the user wants to curate a folder of images into a smaller training set — for character LoRAs, product LoRAs, style LoRAs, or any “pick K best from N candidates” image-selection task. Triggers on “curate these images”, “pick K for LoRA training”, “choose images for character LoRA”, “filter my photo dump”, “select diverse training images”, “build a training set”. Also use to drive lookbook over MCP/HTTP from an agent.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-curate`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-curate).

### `lookbook-dev`

Use when developing or modifying the lookbook package — extending the curation pipeline, adding scorers/selectors/embedders, working with the manifest, swapping storage backends. Triggers on lookbook architecture questions, “how do I add a scorer”, “where does the manifest live”, “what’s the registry pattern”, or any work inside the lookbook repo.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-dev`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-dev).

### `lookbook-diagnose`

Use after a lookbook curation run to interpret the result, explain why specific images were dropped or kept, query the manifest for provenance, or read cluster-coverage diagnoses. Triggers on “why was this image rejected”, “what’s missing from my training set”, “explain the curation report”, “this image was dropped — why”, “what coverage gaps does my set have”.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-diagnose`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-diagnose).

### `lookbook-http`

Use when working on lookbook’s HTTP surface — adding a new endpoint, debugging a route, configuring the server (host/port/data-root), or wiring a frontend/agent client. Triggers on lookbook.http questions, “add an endpoint”, “new HTTP route”, “lookbook serve”, “FastAPI app”, or work in lookbook/http.py.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-http`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-http).

### `lookbook-profile`

Use when adding a new subject profile to lookbook (product, scene, style, brand, font, …). A profile is a YAML file that bundles scorers, embedders, filters, a selector, and constraints into a named recipe. Triggers on “add a profile for X”, “support product LoRAs”, “scene profile”, “style LoRA recipe”, “new subject type”, or work in lookbook/profiles/.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-profile`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-profile).

### `lookbook-recipe`

Use when the user wants to customize a lookbook curation pipeline beyond what the built-in recipes / profiles provide — overriding filter thresholds, swapping selectors, adjusting quotas, building a one-off recipe inline. Triggers on “different defaults”, “custom scorer weights”, “skip aesthetic scoring”, “build my own pipeline”, “tweak the funnel”, “override the threshold”, “what-if reweighting”.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-recipe`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-recipe).

### `lookbook-storage`

Use when working on lookbook persistence — swapping storage backends (filesystem, SQLite, S3, Mongo, Redis), debugging the manifest, designing a new store codec, or wiring stores for tests. Triggers on questions about lookbook.store, get_stores(), the repository pattern, manifest persistence, or “where does lookbook save its data”.

Source: [`.claude/skills/lookbook-storage`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/lookbook/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/lookbook-storage).

# API reference

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
